title: Protocol-Agnostic and Packet-Based Intrusion Detection Using a Multi-Layer Deep-Learning Architecture at the Network Edge
researchArea: Edge Network Intrusion Detection / Protocol-Agnostic Packet Preprocessing
problem: Traditional intrusion detection systems either destroy protocol structure through lossy transformations (e.g., converting packets to images or NLP/Word2Vec embeddings) or suffer from high computational overhead and data sparsity when processing unaligned raw fields across heterogeneous protocols on resource-constrained edge devices.
motivation: Edge computing devices face severe CPU, memory, and battery constraints that prevent running complex deep learning models (such as CNNs or RNNs) or resource-heavy decentralized edge training workflows. Aligning the neural network structure directly with the hierarchical OSI model preserves semantic layer relationships while dramatically reducing computational overhead.
noveltyAndContributions: Designed a dynamic multi-layer deep learning architecture where individual neural networks (NNs) are assigned to specific network protocols (e.g., ETH, IP, TCP, HTTP) and protocol combinations, closely reflecting OSI layer hierarchy.

Proposed a custom, protocol-agnostic Wireshark-driven preprocessing pipeline featuring pattern-matched type inference, categorical heuristics, and 'shadow features' to represent absent protocol fields without arbitrary value imputation.
Demonstrated a lightweight centralized edge training strategy where edge nodes selectively deploy only the sub-networks relevant to their local traffic patterns, optimizing power consumption.
methodology: Grouped raw PCAP network traffic from the CIC-IDS2017 dataset by protocol combinations (e.g., ETH/IP/TCP, ETH/IP/TCP/HTTP).

Extracted packet fields using Wireshark pattern matching to infer custom data types (Long, Address, Float, Label, String, Date, Boolean) and generated shadow feature indicators for conditionally missing fields.

Passed protocol-specific attributes into dedicated protocol NNs (Linear + ReLU + BatchNorm1D), concatenated their output vectors into a fixed-width bridge layer (width = 90), and fed them into combination-specific NNs.
Trained the architecture using Binary Cross-Entropy loss and the Adam optimizer over 150 epochs, automatically tuned via Optuna on Compute Canada GPU clusters.
keyAssumptions: Network packets strictly follow hierarchical OSI layering, allowing individual protocol fields to be processed independently before sub-network concatenation.
Edge devices can periodically receive pre-trained sub-model updates from a central server during maintenance or battery recharge cycles, eliminating local edge training overhead.
datasets: CIC-IDS2017 Dataset (62,029 raw packet subset covering SSH-Patator, FTP-Patator, DoS, Web Attacks, Botnet, DDoS, and Normal traffic)
experimentalSetup: Trained on Compute Canada infrastructure using NVIDIA P100 GPUs with a PostgreSQL database tracking multi-objective trials via Optuna.
80/20 train/test data split evaluated over 150 training epochs with a batch size of 50.
Optimal Hyperparameters: Categorical heuristic = 0.05, Minimum feature percentage = 0.1, Bridge layer width = 90, Adam learning rate = 7.494e-6 (beta1 = 0.6, beta2 = 0.95).
xaiEvaluation: None (The study focuses on structural OSI layer alignment and Wireshark feature type mapping rather than explicit post-hoc XAI methods like SHAP or LIME).
results: Achieved 99.99% across overall Accuracy, F1-Score, Precision, and Recall on the CIC-IDS2017 dataset, outperforming baseline models while significantly reducing model parameter size and packet representation overhead.
failureConditions: Step-like learning variations during hyperparameter optimization caused by individual protocol sub-networks independently reaching local minima before the global combination network converges.
costEvaluation: Decoupling protocol NNs and employing centralized server training reduces edge device battery and computational consumption; edge devices only host and run inference on sub-networks relevant to their specific operational traffic.

limitations.text: The evaluation relies strictly on a centralized server training paradigm rather than a federated or distributed edge learning setup.
The model has not yet been benchmarked against Adversarial Machine Learning (AML) evasion attacks or unlabeled/zero-day threat environments.
Evaluated on an extracted subset (62,029 packets) of CIC-IDS2017 rather than real-world edge IoT topologies or live multi-segment network streams.

futureWork: Explore model compression techniques (pruning and quantization) for resource-constrained edge deployment.
Incorporate adversarial training and unsupervised learning to detect unknown, zero-day attacks.
Integrate intrusion explanation methods (XAI) and benchmark real-time inference latency and memory footprints on edge hardware.
relevance: Directly relevant to your thesis's Layered Intrusion Detection and Heterogeneous Network Segments pillars, providing an OSI-aligned packet parsing framework and demonstrating protocol-agnostic edge sub-network deployment.
newIdeas: Adapt this paper's OSI-aligned modular sub-network architecture into a Federated Learning setup with SHAP feature explainability to evaluate Layer-2 IDS across heterogeneous network segments.
